newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: British, Singaporean firms set Vietnam mission.
newsitem.headline: British, Singaporean firms set Vietnam mission.

text.p: Vietnam's potential for economic growth has attracted trade and investment possibilities from the UK and Singapore, senior representatives announcing a UK-Singapore joint mission to Vietnam said on Thursday.

"This mission to Vietnam shows the commitment of the Singapore-British Business Council (SBBC) to expand bilateral cooperation relations, as well as to jointly seek business and investment opportunities in third country markets," Cheong Quee Wah, co-chairman of the SBBC, said at a news conference.
The mission is jointly organised by SBBC and the Singapore Confederation of Industries.
The mission will include executives from 23 British and Singapore companies who will be in Vietnam June 28 to July 5.
Major participants include Sembawang Engineering and Construction Pte Ltd, Rolls-Royce International, Overseas Union bank, Shell, Temasek Holdings, HSBC Holdings and British Petroleum.

Though the main focus will be on ports and infrastructure development, the mission will also cover environmental consultancy, legal services and project finance. Mission members will attend various networking events while in Hanoi, Haiphong, Hong Gai, Danang and Ho Chi Minh.--Singapore newsroom 65-8703080
